newsitem.title: USA: Dean Foods sees FY Q1 net at about $0.43/shr.
newsitem.headline: Dean Foods sees FY Q1 net at about $0.43/shr.

text.p: Dean Foods Co said Tuesday it expects fiscal first quarter earnings to exceed last year's first quarter results and approximate fiscal first quarter 1995 earnings of $0.43 cents per share.
Dean Foods said it expects to report earnings for its first quarter ending August 25, 1996 on September 19.

Dean Foods had reported earnings of $0.34 a share in its fiscal 1996 first quarter, a quarter which reflected a poor harvest and was not representative of the company's historical results, a company spokesman said.
Dean Foods produces dairy products and ranks third in market share in processed vegetables and first in pickles and specialty products in the U.S.

"Our dairy, pickle and specialty businesses are expected to outperform last year's first quarter results, while the vegetables business will be slightly below last year," Howard Dean, chairman, said in a statement.
"Our dairy and pickle businesses are expected to show significant improvements over the prior year," he said.

Dean Foods' dairy business has benefited from both volume and margin improvements, he said. Its improved pickle business is due to a better spring crop in 1996 and reduced promotional activity, especially in the Southeast, he noted.
Dean Foods said that actions taken last year to improve results will not begin to benefit earnings significantly until late in fiscal 1997 and into fiscal 1998.
Although fiscal 1997 first quarter results are expected to be substantially improved, there are still a number of uncertainties that continue to face the food industry, Dean said in a statement.

Raw milk prices continue to climb and supply has decreased. In addition, the summer crops of vegetables and pickles were late being planted, with less acreage than last year. As a result, future vegetable and pickle costs and pricing, especially frozen vegetables' pricing, could be significantly impacted by the size of this year's harvest.
Dean Foods said it is too early to predict the ultimate impact these uncertainties will have on future earnings.
